source.name: ECDC – European Respiratory Virus Surveillance Summary (ERVISS)
source.publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), an EU agency
source.note: Figures are reported every week by the national public health institutes (FHI, Folkhälsomyndigheten and SSI) to ECDC, which publishes them openly every Friday. Recent weeks can be revised.

findings: Norway: 171 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 42 (+8% on the week before). That is 97% above the average for the same week in the previous 4 seasons (index 197), and higher than in any previous season. Intensity: baseline.

Sweden: 81 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 42 (+62% on the week before). That is 153% above the average for the same week in the previous 4 seasons (index 253), and higher than in any previous season. Intensity: baseline.
Denmark: 87 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 42 (+18% on the week before). That is 91% above the average for the same week in the previous 4 seasons (index 191). Intensity: baseline.
Denmark is above ECDC's epidemic threshold: 12.2% of sentinel samples were positive for influenza in week 42.
Highest influenza level against history: Sweden (index 253, where 100 = historical average).
Dominant influenza virus so far this season (subtyped samples, all three countries): A(H1N1)pdm09 (84%).
Influenza A and B, lab-confirmed cases this week: Norway A 165, B 6; Sweden A 78, B 3; Denmark A 86, B 1.
COVID-19, lab-confirmed cases this week: Norway 167 (+8%, index 27); Sweden 85 (−30%, index 6); Denmark 56 (−5%, index 3).
RSV, lab-confirmed cases this week: Norway 4 (−33%, index 23); Sweden 1 (−67%, index 5); Denmark 0 (–, index 0).
Hospital and severity this week: Sweden 2 deaths with influenza; Sweden 6 deaths with COVID-19.
headline: Influenza: 339 lab-confirmed cases in the Nordics this week, up 20% on last week and above the usual level for the time of year (index 206). Intensity is baseline.
Denmark is above ECDC's epidemic threshold.
Nordics: COVID-19 308 cases (stable, below usual); RSV 5 cases (down 44%, below usual).
